thanks

@JasonBrody2000 I just started using aseprite if I want to just quickly downscale the image and have the texture be really crunchy and because it turns on quicker than photoshop, but normally if I want to add some more details I just use photoshop. Most of the time when you downscale the texture in photoshop its really smoothed out, but you can make them more pixelated if you just convert the image into a smart object before changing the texture size, though I think it still looks better smoothed out on some more natural textures like grass or plants
thanks for the great obj

@JasonBrody2000 I use textures.com for general stuff like grass and brick walls, but for something thats more specific, like the barrels and propane tanks, I just search them up on google and use tool called shoebox to get the part of the texture I want. Then i just edit the contrast, brightness and add rust until Im fine with how it looks, though Im still not sometimes happy with the result. I recommend following any psx tutorial and trying to edit the textures like they do. What really helped me is completing all 3 parts of the summer85 tutorial

"Built in Norway in 1939.

Final Fate - 1940 (Norway still neutral): 

Torpedoed and sunk by U-51 (Knorr) on Jan. 29-1940 on a voyage from Torrevieja, Spain to Aalesund with a cargo of salt, position 43N 10 35W, 16 died, 2 survived. The 2 survivors were rescued from their raft by the U-boat. Eika had been requisitioned by the Norwegian authorities for the voyage to Spain.

A Survivor's Story: 

In the Norwegian magazine "Krigsseileren", Issue No. 1 for 1973 there's an interview with one of the survivors from D/S Eika, Harald Støle (messboy). He and his brother Arne Støle were both on board, Arne as a steward. Harald Støle was 16 years old when he joined in the summer of 1939. He says the torpedo hit just after 15:00 while he and a number of his shipmates were in the messroom having coffee. By the time he got out on deck the ship had broken in 2 and sank right underneath him, taking him down with her, but he was able to get to the surface and grab hold of a raft. Stoker Alfred Johansen from Kopervik was with him, but no one else was to be seen. After a couple of hours the U-boat approached, threw them a line and took them on board where they were given dry clothes. He says they were very well treated on the U-boat and were allowed to wander freely, except in the engine room which was off limits. Harald Støle had his 17th birthday on board on Febr. 4 and on this occasion he was called in to the commander who gave him a drink and some chocolate. He says they spent 11 days on the boat and on arrival Willemshaven they were taken to a military place where they were locked in a room. In the subsequent days they were questioned about D/S Eika and her voyage, Støle even had to make a drawing of the ship. Using that much foot spray would get expensive really quick. Photographing slightly older and used equipment is much easier to model than a brand new machine for obvious reasons. Also shooting on a cloudy day around noon will produce the best models but like you said, this isn't always achievable. One cheaper solution that foot spray is to mix baby powder and rubbing alcohol in a spray bottle. The alcohol will evaporate quickly leaving just the baby powder stuck on the subject.

Nel 1827 si ritrova in una missiva del Ministro Evasio Gozzani destinata al Principe Camillo Borghese tra le opere scelte per essere collocate all’interno delle sale dopo lo spolio Napoleonico. This is honestly the best panda model I’ve been able to find anywhere.

What really impressed me is the level of anatomical accuracy and attention to detail. The pseudo-thumb is correctly included — not just visually, but as a functional structure that would realistically help the panda grip bamboo.

The dental setup is also very well thought out. You can clearly see the 12 incisors (6 upper, 6 lower) used for cutting and peeling, along with the 4 canines that reflect their carnivorous ancestry. Even though the full premolar and molar count isn’t perfectly replicated, the overall structure feels very close to real panda anatomy and remains highly believable.

Beyond accuracy, the model is simply beautiful. The proportions, surface detail, and overall silhouette are very well balanced — realistic without feeling overly complex.

The mesh is clean and well-organized, making it easy to work with in production and showing a high level of technical discipline from the creator.

It’s rare to see a model that combines visual quality, anatomical understanding, and clean structure this well.

Truly excellent work.
